pages.title: Ruins and camps
text: The tribes left more behind than halls and drum circles. Every land of the March has its own remains, most of them with a chest worth opening, and a few guarded by what still walks there.

The deepest of them, the **Old Gate Ruin**, the **Ash Tomb** and the **Crystal Grotto**, keep their best chests behind Hollow Sentinels, and those chests can hold a **Resonant Core** or **Loom Thread**.

pages.title: The Steppe and the Highlands
text: - **Wayfarer's Shrine**: a roofed roadside shrine on an old path, with an offering chest.
- **Grazing Stones**: a ring of standing stones around a salt-lick.
- **Abandoned Waystation**: a ruined relay post, one mast still standing.
- **Fallen Drum Tower**: a broken tower; its great drum lies in the grass.
- **Watchfire Beacon**: a stone tower on a knoll with its signal fire still lit.
- **Echo Quarry**: a terraced pit with March ores in its walls and a crane at the rim.
- **Storm Altar**: a tuff altar under a lightning rod.
- **Seal-Carver's Retreat**: rooms cut into a crag, with a workshop and a loft.
- **Old Gate Ruin**: a half-buried Way Gate over a guarded hall and a barred vault.

pages.title: The Snow Fields and the Ember Wastes
text: - **Frozen Longhall**, **Ice Cairn**, **Hunter's Lodge** and **Aurora Watch** in the snow.
- **Ember Forge**, **Cinder Spire** and **Slag Ring** in the ash, and the **Remnant Den** where survivors held out.
- **Ash Tomb**: a buried tomb under the Wastes, and one of the three deep places worth the risk.

pages.title: The Crystal Fields and the Reed Fen
text: - **Shattered Observatory**: a star-chart terrace under a broken dome.
- **Resonance Obelisk**: a crystal-capped obelisk over a hidden vault.
- **Loom Ruin**: a fallen great loom, cloth still hanging.
- **Crystal Grotto**: a spiral stair down to a geode cave and a vault behind an iron door.
- **Stilt Village**, **Sunken Shrine**, **Reed Weir** and **Bog Barrow** in the fen.
- **Spirit Well**: a roofed well ringed with blooms, its offering chest at the bottom of the water.
